title: Adaptive prefetch quarantine and path rewrite to stabilize token throughput
creator: Asha Patel
description: Summary: Multiple enterprise customers reported intermittent initial-token stalls (TTFT) followed by rapid tokens/sec degradation across hosted, dedicated, and private clusters when high model-fanout and aggressive prefetch patterns coincide. Impact: production latency SLO breaches (TTFT spike + sustained tokens/sec drop) on mixed-precision and quantized variants; observed elevated KV eviction churn on serving nodes. Hypothesis: a subset of prefetch requests with long context prefixes cause synchronous KV prefetch that competes with active token generation for memory bandwidth and kernel scheduling, triggering eviction thrash and degraded token throughput across colocated contexts. Goal: implement a conservative quarantine for suspicious prefetches and an adaptive path rewrite that routes flagged requests to a low-priority prefetch lane or to a compatible model-variant with reduced KV pressure, restoring steady tokens/sec and preventing cross-tenant impact. Non-goals: we will not change kernel selection heuristics in this task; that work is owned by a follow-up (ENG-712345).

acceptance_criteria: Canary demonstrates sustained tokens/sec at or above baseline for two production-like workloads for 24h
No regression in median TTFT for non-flagged requests across hosted/dedicated/private regions
Prefetch-quarantine metrics emit spans and counters that allow SRE to verify isolation events
Runbook updated with rollback steps and runbook drill completed by SRE team
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (canary): implement quarantine flagging + low-priority prefetch lane + path rewrite to fallback model-variant; deploy to two dedicated pools
Phase 2 (observe): monitor TTFT/tokens/sec/kv-eviction for 24-48h; tune threshold heuristics
Phase 3 (ramp): A/B rollout across hosted and private with gradual traffic ramp and customer opt-in toggle
Phase 4 (followups): hand off kernel selection and eviction-policy work to follow-ups (ENG-712345, ENG-481924)
risk_assessment: Medium-high: changes affect request routing and prefetch scheduling; mitigations include conservative default thresholds, canary-first rollout, and immediate rollback path. There is a risk of increased latency for quarantined requests (expected trade-off) which will be communicated to customers during rollouts.
rollout_notes: Default is disabled for private clusters until ops approves. Hosted/Dedicated will use an adaptive 10% traffic canary, doubled every 12h if no regressions. Provide customer opt-out and per-customer threshold override in Console.
